en: One who has recently come to a community; a recent arrival.
A new participant in some activity; a neophyte.

newcomer.ety: From Middle English newe-comere, equivalent to new- + comer. Compare Old English nīwcumen (“new comer, neophyte, novice”).

ex.en: The newcomer carried off the first prize.
ex.ja: 新来者が１等賞をさらった。

ex.en: The newcomer sat down at the foot of the table.
ex.ja: 新しく来た人は末席についた。

ex.en: Isn't it nice when the newcomers are still so innocent?
ex.ja: やっぱり新人さんは初々しくていいね。

note.ja: new（新しく）+ comer（来た人）。「新しく来た人」。

Methodical or systematic.
A hospital attendant given a variety of non-medical duties.
A soldier who carries out minor tasks for a superior officer.

ex.ja: 私は規則正しい生活をしている。

ex.ja: 規則正しい生活、食事が健康の秘訣です。

en: An onset; the beginning or initial stage of something.

outset.ety: From out- + set, replacing earlier outsetting.

ex.en: You should have mentioned it at the outset.
ex.ja: あなたはそれを初めに言っとくべきだった。

ex.en: The meeting was held as intended at the outset.
ex.ja: その会合は当初の予定どおりに開催された。

ex.en: There isn't anyone who knows everything from the outset.
ex.ja: 初めから何でも知っている人などいません。

note.ja: out（外へ）+ set（据える）。「出発すること」→「最初」。

en: Partly or wholly incapable of movement; disabled.
Rendered incapable of action.

ex.en: He was paralyzed in the face of danger.
ex.ja: 彼は危険に直面して身動きできなかった。

ex.en: The general strike paralyzed the whole country.
ex.ja: ゼネストで国中の機能が麻痺した。

ex.en: The child was paralyzed with fear.
ex.ja: その子供は恐怖で身動きができなかった。

note.ja: paralyze（麻痺させる）+ -ed。ギリシャ語 paralysis ＝ para（横に）+ lyein（ゆるめる）。「麻痺した」。analysis と同じ ly。

en: To avoid, deflect, or ward off (an attack, a blow, an argument, etc.).
A defensive or deflective action; an act of parrying.
A simple defensive action designed to deflect an attack, performed with the forte of the blade.

parry.ety:
From earlier parree, from Middle English *parree, *paree, from Old French paree (“preparation, ceremony, parade”), from Medieval Latin parāta (“preparation, parade”), from parāre (“to ward off, guard, defend, prepare, get ready”). More at pare. The English verb is taken from the noun. Doublet of parade.
Alternative etymology derives the verb parry from French parez, the imperative form of parer (“to fend off”), ultimately from the Medieval Latin parāre. See above.

note.ja: フランス語 parer（受け止める）から。「（攻撃を）受け流す」。parachute の para（防ぐ）と同じ。

en: A paved outside area, adjoining a house, used for dining or recreation.
An inner courtyard typical of traditional houses in some regions of Spain.

patio.ety: From Spanish patio, either from Old Occitan patu or pati (compare Occitan and Catalan pati), of uncertain origin.

ex.en: Do you have a table in the patio?
ex.ja: 中庭の席がありますか。

ex.en: Do you have a table on the patio?
ex.ja: 中庭の席がありますか。

ex.en: I thought we could eat out on the patio.
ex.ja: 私たちは中庭で食べることができると思っていました。

note.ja: スペイン語 patio（中庭）から。「テラス・中庭」。

To strut about proudly or haughtily.
To engage in peacocking, ostentatious dress or behaviour to impress women.

en: A power station; the building housing the core parts of a power station, such as the dynamo.
Any source of power, energy or strength; a source of influence or inspiration.

note.ja: power + house。「発電所」→「原動力・実力者」。

en: That which precurses: a forerunner, predecessor, or indicator of approaching events.
One of the compounds that participates in the chemical reaction that produces another compound.
Caused by the following symbol.

precursor.ety: Inherited from Middle English precursour, from Middle French precurseur or its etymon Latin praecursor (“forerunner”). By surface analysis, precurse + -or.

note.ja: pre（前に）+ curs（走る）+ or。前を走るもの →「先駆者・前兆」。

en: Better than some other option; preferred.

preferable.ety: From prefer + -able, probably after Middle French preferable. Compare preference, preferential, etc.

ex.en: It is preferable that she do it alone.
ex.ja: 彼女はひとりでやるのが望ましい。

ex.en: I think death is preferable to shame.
ex.ja: 私は恥より死のほうがましだと思っている。

ex.en: Bad news is preferable to an absence of information.
ex.ja: 情報がないより悪い知らせでもあるほうがまだましだ。

note.ja: prefer（好む）+ -able。「好ましい」。

en: Of or pertaining to preparation, having the purpose of making something or someone ready, preparative.

preparatory.ety: From Middle English preparatori, from Late Latin praeparatorius. By surface analysis, prepare + -atory.

note.ja: prepare + -atory。「準備の」→ prep school（進学校）。

A cutting (“open passage at a level lower than the surrounding terrain, dug for a canal, railway, or road to go through”) or an embankmen…

ex.en: Light is resolved by a prism into seven colors.
ex.ja: 光線はプリズムによって七色に分解される。

ex.en: A prism decomposes light.
ex.ja: プリズムは光を分解する。

ex.en: How many vertices and faces does a pentagonal prism have?
ex.ja: 五角柱の頂点の数と面の数は，それぞれいくつですか。

en: A statement which is proclaimed; a formal public announcement.

proclamation.ety: From Middle English proclamacion, from Anglo-Norman and Old French proclamacion, from Late Latin proclāmātiō, from the verb Latin prōclāmō.

note.ja: pro（前で）+ clam（叫ぶ）+ ation。人前で叫ぶこと →「宣言・布告」。proclaim（宣言する）。

en: One who supports something; an advocate.
One who makes a proposal or proposition.
Making proposals; proposing.

proponent.ety: From Latin prōpōnēns, present participle of prōpōnō (“to put forward; propose”).

ex.en: Proponents of increased import duties are at odds with each other.
ex.ja: 関税引き上げの提案国はお互いに反目しています。

note.ja: ラテン語 proponere（前に置く・提案する）から。「提唱者・支持者」。propose と同じ pon。opponent の対。

en: Serving or tending to elicit a strong, often negative sentiment in another person; exasperating.
Serving or tending to excite, stimulate or arouse sexual interest; sexy.
Something that provokes an appetite, especially a sexual appetite; an aphrodisiac.

provocative.ety: Borrowed from Middle French provocatif, and its source, Late Latin provocativus, from Latin provocare.

ex.en: Mary is wearing provocative clothing.
ex.ja: メアリーはきわどい格好をしている。

ex.en: After seeing her provocative body, he became obsessed with her.
ex.ja: 彼女の悩ましげな姿を見て、彼はすっかり夢中になってしまいました。

note.ja: provoke（挑発する）+ -ative。pro + vocare（呼ぶ）。「呼び出す」→「挑発的な」。voice と同じ voc。

en: On purpose; intentionally.

purposely.ety: From Middle English purposly; equivalent to purpose + -ly.

ex.en: She purposely showed off her dress.
ex.ja: 彼女はわざとドレスを見せびらかした。

note.ja: purpose（目的）+ -ly。「わざと」。

en: To return land to a suitable condition for use.
To obtain useful products from waste; to recycle.
An effort to take something back, to reclaim something.
Material recovered from something that has already been used.

ex.en: Some day man will reclaim the desert for agriculture.
ex.ja: いつの日か人間は砂漠を開拓して農業に利用するだろう。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ claim（要求する）。「取り戻す」→ 土地を「埋め立てる」。

ex.ja: 駅前の再開発が進んで、新しいお店が増えてきた。

note.ja: re（再び）+ development（開発）。「再開発」。

en: An automatic response to a simple stimulus which does not require mental processing.
The descendant of an earlier language element, such as a word or phoneme, in a daughter language.
Bent, turned back or reflected.
Produced automatically by a stimulus.
To bend back or turn back over itself.
To respond to a stimulus.

reflex.ety: From Late Latin reflexus, past participle of reflectere (“to bend back”), equivalent to re- + flex. Photography sense is from noun sense meaning “reflection”. Compare English reflect.

ex.ja: その少年は運動神経が発達している。

ex.en: He has excellent reflexes.
ex.ja: 彼は運動神経が抜群だ。

ex.en: Boxers need quick reflexes.
ex.ja: ボクサーにはすばやい身のこなしが必要だ。

note.ja: re（後ろへ）+ flex（曲げる）。跳ね返るように曲がること →「反射（作用）」。reflect（反射する）。

A reunion of a former couple into a new relationship.
To bring opponents together for such a contest.

The money or other item that is repaid.

en: Eggs of fish.
Sperm of certain fish.

roe.ety:

en: The broken remains of an object, usually rock or masonry.
A mass or stratum of fragments of rock lying under the alluvium and derived from the neighbouring rock.
To break down into rubble.

rubble.ety: Inherited from Middle English rouble, rubel, robel, robeil, from Anglo-Norman *robel (“bits of broken stone”). ex.en: There is a large pile of rubble where the school building used to be.
ex.ja: 校舎の跡地は瓦礫の山となっている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 robe（略奪品）とされる。rubbish と同系。「がれき」。

A white, yellow, or purple variety of corundum, either clear or translucent.
of a deep blue colour.
pertaining to a 45th year

A suture.
To put together with a seam.
To make the appearance of a seam in, as in knitting a stocking; hence, to knit with a certain stitch, like that in such knitting.

lagoon.ety: Borrowed from French lagune, from Italian laguna, from Latin lacūna. Related to Old English lagu via Proto-Indo-European. Doublet of lacuna and lacune.

note.ja: イタリア語 laguna（潟）から。ラテン語 lacuna（くぼみ・池）。lake と同系。

en: A wound or injury.
An infected or otherwise injured or diseased organ or part, especially such on a patch of skin.
To wound or injure, especially in an experiment or other controlled procedure.

lesion.ety: From Middle English lesioun (“physical injuring of the body”), from Old French lesion (“hurt, offense, wrong, injury, wound”), from Latin laesiō (“hurt, harm, injury”) (whence -ion (“noun suffix denoting action, result, process, state, condition”)), from laesus (“hurt, injured, wounded, damaged”), past participle of laedō (“to strike, collide, hurt”).

note.ja: ラテン語 laesio（傷つけること）から。laedere（傷つける）。「病変・損傷」。

en: To walk lamely, as if favoring one leg.
To travel with a malfunctioning system of propulsion.
An irregular, jerky or awkward gait.
A scraper for removing poor ore or refuse from the sieve.
Flaccid; flabby, resembling flesh.
Lacking stiffness; floppy, flimsy.

limp.ety:
From Middle English limpen (“to fall short”), from Old English limpan, from Proto-West Germanic *limpan, from Proto-Germanic *limpaną (“to hang down”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)lemb-, *(s)lembʰ- (“to hang loosely, hang limply”).
Cognate with Low German lumpen (“to limp”), Middle High German limpfen (“to hobble, limp”), dialectal German lampen (“to hang down loosely”), Icelandic limpa (“limpness, weakness”).

ex.en: An old woman limped along the street.
ex.ja: １人の老婆が不自由な足で通りを歩いていた。

ex.en: The hat got wet and went limp.
ex.ja: 帽子がぬれてふにゃふにゃになった。

ex.en: The German Shepherd was limping down the street.
ex.ja: そのシェパードは、びっこをひきながら道を歩いていた。

note.ja: 古英語 lemphealt（足の不自由な）から。「足を引きずる」。

ex.ja: 彼女は合理的な考え方をする人です。

ex.ja: 論理的に考えるのが苦手。

en: An insane person.
Crazed, mad, insane, demented.

lunatic.ety: From Middle English lunatik, from Old French lunatique, from Late Latin lunaticus (“moonstruck”), derived from Latin luna (“moon”), the connection stemming from the belief that changes of the moon caused intermittent insanity.

ex.en: He acted like a lunatic.
ex.ja: 彼は狂人のように振る舞った。

note.ja: ラテン語 lunaticus（月の影響を受けた）から。luna（月）。月の満ち欠けで狂気が起こると考えられた。lunar と同じ。

Expressive of emotion.

en: The act or process of becoming manifest.
The embodiment of an intangible, or variable thing.

manifestation.ety: From Middle English manifestacion, manyfestacion, manyfestacioun; from Late Latin manifestātiō. In the political sense, a semantic loan from French manifestation. By surface analysis, manifest + -ation.

ex.en: It is a manifestation of her expectations.
ex.ja: それは彼女の期待の現れです。

en: An alcoholic drink fermented from honey and water.
A drink composed of syrup of sarsaparilla or other flavouring extract, and water, and sometimes charged with carbon dioxide.

mead.ety:
From Middle English mede, from Old English medu, from Proto-West Germanic *medu, from Proto-Germanic *meduz, from Proto-Indo-European *médʰu (“honey; honey wine”).
Cognate with Ancient Greek μέθυ (méthu) (whence English methyl), Lithuanian medùs, Old Church Slavonic медъ (medŭ, “honey”), Persian می (mey), Sanskrit मधु (mádhu), Welsh medd, Finnish mesi, Chinese 蜜 (mì).

note.ja: 古英語 meodu（蜂蜜酒）から。

en: To relocate periodically from one region to another, usually according to the seasons.
To change one's geographic pattern of habitation.

migrate.ety: First attested in 1623; borrowed from Latin migrātus, perfect passive participle of migrō (“to migrate, change, transport”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix).

ex.en: Why do birds migrate in the first place?
ex.ja: そもそもなぜ鳥は移動するのだろうか。

ex.en: These birds migrate to North Africa in winter.
ex.ja: これらの鳥は冬には北アフリカに渡る。

ex.en: Early man migrated to all parts of the world.
ex.ja: 初期の人類は世界のあらゆる所に移住した。

note.ja: ラテン語 migrare（移る）から。→「移住する・（鳥が）渡る・（データを）移行する」。

en: In a mild manner.
To a mild degree; slightly.

English -ly

From mild + -ly.

ex.en: He has too many interests, to put it mildly.
ex.ja: 控え目に言っても彼は関心事が多すぎる。

ex.en: That's putting it mildly.
ex.ja: それは控え目に言ってるんだよ。

ex.en: I was mildly disappointed.
ex.ja: 私は少しがっかりした。

note.ja: mild + -ly。「穏やかに・少し」→ to put it mildly（控えめに言っても）。

en: By supernatural or uncommon causes, e.g. by a god; that cannot be explained in terms of normal events.
Very surprising; amazing.

miraculous.ety: From Middle French miraculeux. Displaced native Old English wundorlīċ.

ex.en: Tom made a miraculous recovery.
ex.ja: トムは奇跡的な回復を遂げた。

ex.en: This, the first of the miraculous signs, Jesus performed in Cana in Galilee.
ex.ja: イエスはこのことを最初のしるしとしてガリラヤのカナで行った。

note.ja: miracle（奇跡）+ -ous。ラテン語 mirari（驚く）。「奇跡的な」。

en: A set of moral norms or customs derived from generally accepted practices rather than written laws.

mores.ety: From Latin mōrēs (“ways, character, morals”), the plural of mōs. Doublet of moeurs.

note.ja: ラテン語 mos（習慣）の複数形。「慣習・道徳観」。moral と同じ。

en: To express sadness or sorrow for; to grieve over (especially a death).
To engage in the social customs of mourning; to commemorate a death and/or honour the deceased socially.
Sorrow, grief.
A ring fitted upon the head of a lance to prevent wounding an adversary in tilting.

mourn.ety: From Middle English mornen, mournen, from Old English murnan, from Proto-Germanic *murnaną. Cognate with French morne (“gloomy”).

ex.en: She mourned the death of her only son.
ex.ja: 彼女は一人息子の死をいたみ悲しんだ。

ex.en: The whole neighborhood mourned his death.
ex.ja: 近所の人々はみな彼の死をいたみ悲しんだ。

ex.en: We all mourned for the people killed in the accident.
ex.ja: 私たちは皆事故による死者に哀悼の意を表した。

note.ja: 古英語 murnan（嘆く）から。「嘆く・悼む」。mourning と同じ。

en: Worldly, earthly, profane, vulgar as opposed to heavenly.
Pertaining to the Universe, cosmos or physical reality, as opposed to the spiritual world.
An unremarkable, ordinary human being.
A person with no magical or supernatural powers or properties.

mundane.ety:
From Middle English mondeyne, from Old French mondain, from Late Latin mundānus, from Latin mundus (“world”). Compare Danish mondæn.
(ordinary): Compare typologically Russian несусве́тный (nesusvétnyj) (<~ не- (ne-) + (rare) сусве́тный (susvétnyj) < свет (svet)).

note.ja: ラテン語 mundus（世界）から。「この世の」→「平凡な・日常の」。

en: A vote against.
A person who voted against.

nay.ety:
From Middle English nai, nei, from Old Norse nei (“no”), contraction of ne (“not”) + ei (“ever”), itself from Proto-Germanic *nai (“never”), *nē (“not”). More at no.
The verb is from Middle English nayen (“to refuse, deny, gainsay”), from the interjection and adverb above.

ex.en: Nay, then, I will try it.
ex.ja: いや、それなら僕がやってみよう。

note.ja: 北欧語 nei（いいえ）から。no と同系。「いや（むしろ）・反対票」。

en: The shell that surrounds the kernel of a nut.
A short book summarizing an area of law.
To summarize.

nutshell.ety:
From Middle English notschelle, from Old English hnutsċiell, from Proto-West Germanic *hnutskallju, equivalent to nut + shell. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Nuteskele, Nuteskil (“nutshell”), Dutch notenschaal (“nutshell”), German Nussschale (“nutshell”).
The verb, as well as the legal book sense, is in reference to the phrase in a nutshell (“summarized”).

ex.en: That's it in a nutshell.
ex.ja: 早い話が、そういうことですな。

note.ja: nut（木の実）+ shell（殻）。「クルミの殻」→ 殻に入るほど小さく →「要するに（in a nutshell）」。

en: Prone to cause obsession.
Having one thought or pursuing one activity (an obsession) to the absolute or nearly absolute exclusion of all others.
A person who is obsessed, who has an obsession.

ex.ja: この問題は、アイドルのエゴとヲタのエゴの衝突だ。

note.ja: obsess + -ive。「強迫的な」。

en: Outside of a boat; in the water.
Over the edge; especially, off or outside of a boat.
Excessively; too much.
To throw over the edge of a boat into the water.
To cover (a ceiling) with plasterboard to create a new surface.

overboard.ety: From Middle English overbord, overborde, equivalent to over- + board.

ex.en: John sometimes goes overboard in drinking.
ex.ja: ジョンは時々たくさん酒を飲む。

ex.en: He's given to going overboard every time he gets a new idea.
ex.ja: 何か新しい考えを思いつくたびに、彼は前後の見境もなくそれを実行する傾向がある。

ex.en: I went overboard about the Beatles when I was young.
ex.ja: 若いころ私はビートルズに夢中になった。

note.ja: over（越えて）+ board（船べり）。「船外へ」→ go overboard（度を越す）。

en: A supporting post attached to the main rafter.
A piece of jewellery which hangs down as an ornament, especially worn on a chain around the neck.

pendant.ety: From Anglo-Norman pendaunt, Middle French pendant, noun use of adjective.

ex.en: I bought a pendant to wear to the party.
ex.ja: 私はパーティーにしていくペンダントを買った。

ex.en: I'll give you this pendant.
ex.ja: 君にこのペンダントをあげるよ。

ex.en: My aunt gave me the pendant I'm wearing.
ex.ja: 私が付けているペンダントは叔母さんからもらった。

note.ja: pend（ぶら下がる）+ ant。ぶら下がっているもの →「ペンダント・垂れ飾り」。

en: Fairly short and of slim build.
Of small size; intended for small-framed adult women.
A mutant first discovered in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, forming small colonies when grown in the presence of fermentable carbon …

petite.ety: Borrowed from French petite f, feminine of petit m (“small, little”).

note.ja: フランス語 petit（小さい）の女性形。「小柄な」。petty（ささいな）と同じ。

en: Someone who solicits customers for prostitution and acts as manager for a group of prostitutes; a pander.
To act as a procurer of prostitutes; to pander.
To prostitute someone.
Five in Cumbrian and Welsh sheep counting.

pimp.ety: Origin unknown. Perhaps from French pimpant (“smart, sparkish”) or German Pimpf (“a boy, a youth, a young squirt”). The Old English near-synonym was rendered by Old English forspennend (literally “a solicitor”).

ex.en: The pimp was arrested for human trafficking.
ex.ja: その売春仲介人は人身売買の罪で逮捕された。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。「売春仲介人」→（俗）「派手に飾る」。

en: Possessing poise, having self-confidence.
Ready, prepared.

note.ja: poise（釣り合わせる）+ -ed。ラテン語 pensare（重さを量る）。「釣り合った」→「落ち着いた・準備ができた」。

Next to, or facing the main stem or axis.
The posterior portions of the human body; especially, the buttocks.
The probability that a hypothesis is true (calculated by Bayes' theorem).

An organic pocket in which a marsupial carries its young.
To enclose within a pouch.
To transport within a pouch, especially a diplomatic pouch.

ex.ja: カンガルーの雌は子供を腹の袋に入れて動く。

en: Ability, skill, competence.

proficiency.ety: From proficient or its etymon, Latin prōficiēns (present participle of prōficiō), + -ency.

ex.en: The letters STEP stand for the Society for Testing English Proficiency.
ex.ja: ＳＴＥＰという文字は日本英語検定協会を表している。

ex.en: He has increased his proficiency in English greatly.
ex.ja: 彼は非常に英語に熟達してきた。

ex.ja: 彼女は急速に英語力が伸びた。

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ fic（作る）+ iency。前へ作り進めること →「熟達・技能」。proficient（熟達した）。

en: Of, related to, or suffering from psychosis.
Out of control, bizarre, or crazy.
A person affected by psychosis.

psychotic.ety: Derived in English from psychosis + -tic; compare French psychotique, German psychotisch. Attested from the late 19th century. Compare earlier neurotic.

note.ja: psychosis（精神病）+ -tic。ギリシャ語 psykhē（心）。「精神病の」。

demotion in a hierarchy, for example in business

en: A list of dramas, operas, pieces, parts, etc., which a company or a person has rehearsed and is prepared to perform or display.
The set of skills, abilities, experiences, etc., possessed by a person.

repertoire.ety: Borrowed from French répertoire, from Middle French repertoire, from Late Latin repertōrium (“an inventory, list, repertory”). Doublet of repertory.

note.ja: フランス語 répertoire（目録）から。ラテン語 reperire（見つける）。「演目一覧」→「レパートリー」。

en: A location for storage, often for safety or preservation.
A storage location for files, such as downloadable software packages, or files in a source control system.

repository.ety: From Middle English reposytorye, from Latin repositōrium. By surface analysis, reposit + -ory.

note.ja: ラテン語 repositorium（保管所）から。re + ponere（置く）。「保管場所・宝庫」。deposit と同じ pos。

en: A low, heavy, continuous sound, such as that of thunder or a hungry stomach.
A rotating cask or box in which small articles are smoothed or polished by friction against each other.
To make a low, heavy, continuous sound.
To discover deceitful or underhanded behaviour.
An onomatopoeia describing a rumbling noise

rumble.ety:
From Middle English rumblen, romblen, rummelyn, frequentative form of romen (“to roar”), equivalent to rome + -le. Cognate with Dutch rommelen (“to rumble”), Low German rummeln (“to rumble”), German rumpeln (“to be noisy”), Danish rumle (“to rumble”), all of imitative origin.
Compare typologically Russian громи́ть (gromítʹ), погро́м (pogróm), разгро́м (razgróm) (akin to гром (grom), греме́ть (gremétʹ), громыха́ть (gromyxátʹ)). Also compare гро́хнуть (gróxnutʹ) (akin to гро́хот (gróxot)).

ex.en: My stomach is rumbling.
ex.ja: 胃がごろごろ音をたてます。

ex.en: In the distance the thunder is rumbling.
ex.ja: 遠くで雷がゴロゴロいってるよ。

ex.en: The thunder is rumbling in the distance.
ex.ja: 遠くで雷がゴロゴロいってるよ。

note.ja: 中英語 romblen から。擬音的な語。「ゴロゴロ鳴る」→（俗）けんか。

en: A tavern, especially in an American Old West setting.
A car with a boot or trunk compartment separate from the driver/passenger space and with seating and doors for more than two people.

saloon.ety: From Occitan salon, French salon, either augmentative of salle (“room”), or borrowed from Italian salone (“hall”), augmentative form of sala, salla (“room”); in both cases borrowed from a Germanic source such as Old High German sal (“house, hall”), from Proto-Germanic *salą, from Proto-Indo-European *sel- (“dwelling”). Doublet of salon.

note.ja: フランス語 salon（大広間）から。「大広間」→ 西部の「酒場」→（英）セダン型自動車。salon と同じ。

en: A crude, roughly built hut or cabin.
Any poorly constructed or poorly furnished building.
To live (in or with); to shack up.

shack.ety:
Unknown. Some scholars derive this word from Mexican Spanish jacal, from Nahuatl xacalli (“adobe hut”).
Alternatively, the word may instead come from ramshackle/ramshackly (e.g., old ramshackly house) or perhaps it may be a back-formation from shackly.
Compare Tavringer Romani hak (“place, house”), Traveller Norwegian hak (“place”).

ex.ja: 掘っ建て小屋でもいいから自分の家が欲しい。

ex.en: Why aren't you going to the sugar shack? Because we're all busy.
ex.ja: どうして製糖所に行かないの？私たちは皆忙しいですから。

note.ja: メキシコのスペイン語 jacal（小屋）とされる。「掘っ立て小屋」。

An unregenerate person.

A male animal that has fathered a particular offspring (especially used of domestic animals and in biological research).
To father; to beget.

corona.ety:
The noun is borrowed from Latin corōna (“crown; garland, wreath”), from Ancient Greek κορώνη (korṓnē, “type of crown; curved object (door handle, tip of a bow, stern of a ship, etc.)”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to turn, bend”). The English word is a doublet of crown, korona, koruna, krona, króna, and krone.
The plural form coronae is borrowed from Latin corōnae.
The verb is derived from the noun.

ex.en: I will not take the Corona vaccine.
ex.ja: コロナワクチンは受けないよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 corona（冠）から。太陽の外側の光の冠 →「コロナ」。crown、coronation と同じ。

en: To grow plants, notably crops.

Cognates include Ancient Greek πέλω (pélō) and Sanskrit चरति (cárati). The same Proto-Indo-European root also gave Latin in-quil-īnus (“inhabitant”) and anculus (“servant”).

ex.ja: 絵本は子供たちの頭を啓発する。

ex.en: We should cultivate our minds by reading good books.
ex.ja: 我々は良書を読んで心を養わねばならない。

ex.en: Anyone can cultivate their interest in music.
ex.ja: 誰でも音楽に対する興味を育てる事が出来ます。

note.ja: cult（耕す）+ iv + ate。耕す →「栽培する・（能力を）養う・（関係を）築く」。

en: To challenge (someone) or brave (a hazard or opposition).
To refuse to obey.

defy.ety: From Old French desfier, from Vulgar Latin *disfidare (“renounce one's faith”), from Latin dis- (“away”) + fidus (“faithful”). Meaning shifted in the 14th century from "be disloyal" to "challenge". Contrast confide, fidelity, faith.

ex.ja: 彼が黙っているのは罪を犯している事を意味していると思いますか。

ex.ja: 何も元を持たない集合は空集合と呼ばれ、{}と表される。

en: Completely without; having none of

en: Any female celebrity, usually a well known singer or actress.

diva.ety: From Italian diva (“diva, goddess”), from Latin dīva (“goddess”), female of dīvus (“divine, divine one; notably a deified mortal”), from Old Latin deivā, from Proto-Italic *deiwā (“goddess”), feminine of *deiwos (“god”), from Proto-Indo-European *deywós (“god”).

ex.en: Mary was referred to as the diva of the century.
ex.ja: メアリーは世紀の歌姫と呼ばれていた。

note.ja: イタリア語 diva（女神）から。ラテン語 divus（神の）。「歌姫」。divine と同じ。

en: To turn aside from a course.
To distract.

divert.ety: From Middle English diverten, Old French divertir (“to turn or go different ways, part, separate, divert”), from Latin di- (“apart”) + vertere (“to turn”); see verse.

ex.ja: 彼女は様々の不安から気を紛らわせることができた。

en: A person or animal who eats.
A fruit or other food that is suitable for eating, especially one that is intended to be eaten uncooked.

eater.ety: From Middle English eter, etere, etter, from Old English etere; equivalent to eat + -er (agent noun suffix) or + -er (patient suffix) (food suitable for eating).

ex.en: What a big eater he is!
ex.ja: 彼はなんて大食らいなんだろう。

ex.en: He is a big eater.
